requirements.authoring:
Onto syntax: object CamelCase then indented fields, e.g. name: string @required, amount: int @required, policy: Policy @required. Type constraints use @rule Type.amount is at least 0. A derived field uses field: int = expression. Foundation actors already exist: do not redeclare them. story Title contains indented Actor verb Object, then further indented requires Object.field is ... and sets Object.field to ... . Use creates for creation; a gate on the new object's fields can make a beat refer to an existing object instead, so constrain creation with type @rule or an existing participant. A creation participant is written Actor creates Item for Policy, with sets Item.policy to Policy. Policies can be objects modified by Stories using sets; guards can compare Item.amount is at most Item.policy.limit. Mutation must write an explicit sets clause. A seed block is seed Type followed by one row per instance, e.g. name: "main", limit: 10. Seed references use the named record's name. Runtime commands use Type:name IDs and integer stored units. A Story-written status enum needs complete lifecycle and @final ending; use numeric or boolean fields if no lifecycle is needed. Booleans are true/false. Numbers use int, not integer or number. Cross-type links should have mirrors. Every named participant must be used in a clause. Every clause type must be bound by the sentence, a stored path, or finds. No System or every Stories. No external effects. No imports. Do not output markdown fences. Return only the source/error response schema. Important: story block titles are arbitrary short identifiers; the executable sentence must be indented beneath the block title and match the requested operation exactly. Never put the operation only in the block title. A seeded name needs a declared name: string @required on objects. Do not assign creation inputs to themselves. story Inventory

seed Stock
  name: "shelf", available: 1

For a creation beat with a participant, the entire sentence (e.g. Operator creates Ticket for Queue) belongs under a story block, with sets Ticket.queue to Queue one level further indented.
